findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed knife sanitizing dip well to have no level of detectable chlorine in solution. Discussed possible causes with PIC. PIC stated that the sanitizer was prepared at 8:00am. Discussed evaporation of CL and also sanitizer reduction with use of sanitizer. PIC changed out the sanitizer immediately for solution measuring 100 PPM CL. Ensure solution is tested regularly to prevent food contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. findings.citation_text: 750.540 - Establishment does not currently have any full-time licensed food service sanitation mangers on staff. Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager. Store manager took the food sanitation test last week. If the information is not provided prior to 2/8/11, the routine inspection in 2011 will also count as a follow up inspection and will result in a charge of $75.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.citation_text: 750.100 - Meatballs leftover from Sunday were being reheated for service on Monday morning. The establishment is medium risk and can not cool and reheat foods for more then one days use. Any hot foods (gravy, soups, meatballs, etc.) heated for use must be served or discarded in the same day and can not be reused for multiple days. Any hot foods that are leftover must be discarded at the end of the day. The establishment must upgrade to high risk if foods are going are being cooled and reheated for multiple day use. Meatballs were removed from steam table to be discarded.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text: 750.210 Meatballs were being reheated in the steam table and were 57F-81F. Meatballs, gravy, soups and other foods that will be held hot must first be rapidly heated in the microwave. The steam table is meant to hold hot foods at 135F/above once they have already been heated to appropriate temperatures. When a commercially processed product is first opened it must be heated to a minimum of 135F and any product not heated from the original packaging must be heated to 165F for use before placing on the steam table. The meatballs were removed from the steam table to be discarded.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.650 - Lids on containers of vegetables in 2 door cooler were severely cracked. All food contact surfaces must be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices. Lids in question were discarded, and containers of food were covered with lids that were in good repair.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) top inside microwave (crusty food splash); B) (R) soda nozzles & diffusers (mold); C) back/sides of soda machine ice shoot (mold); & D) knife in crevice between hotdog cooker & bun warmer (crusty food debris). Wash, rinse, and sanitize the above items and all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to eliminate buildup of mold and food debris. Also, do not store utensils in crevices of equipment.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - Paper towels were not available at the back handsink; the dispenser appeared to be jammed. Also, the basin to the back handsink was soiled (slimy debris). Soap and paper towels must be available at all handsinks to allow for proper handwashing. Handsinks and dispensers for soap and paper towels must be kept clean. Clean the basin and provide paper towels at the handsink in question.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 - The door sweep on the back door had gaps in the corners where light from the outside was visible. Outer openings must be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects. Repair the back door so it is tight fitting.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.citation_text: 750.1310 - Bottle of multi-surface cleaner was observed hanging on a rack next to/above bags of chips. All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food, single service items, & clean equipment) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals. Spray bottle of cleaner was moved to the floor next to the make table.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.citation_text: 750.540 - Establishment does not currently have any full-time licensed food service sanitation mangers on staff. All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager. Store manager recently started taking the class to get his license.
